title: Heat-shrink a sleeve over a crimped cable lug: one hand turns the cable, the other works a heat gun along it
instruction: Switch the heat gun on, shrink the sleeve over the lug and cable with it, then put the gun back in its stand, switch it off and move both hands away.
context: Electricians (O*NET 47-2111.00) list as Core tasks 'Install ground leads and connect power cables to equipment, such as motors.' and 'Assemble, install, test, or maintain electrical or electronic wiring, equipment, appliances, apparatus, or fixtures, using hand tools or power tools.' A power-cable termination is commonly finished with an adhesive-lined heat-shrink sleeve over the crimped lug. TE's heating steps (114-120022): 'Start to shrink the tubing starting from one end of the assembly. Work progressively to the end of the tubing ensuring uniform heat application. This can be achieved by either rotating the assembly or the heat gun. Ensure that the end of the heat gun does not touch the exterior of the tubing.' One hand holds the cable by its jacket and turns it; the other switches the gun on and works its jet along the sleeve (moving the gun, or the cable through it), so every side of every part recovers, without lingering until it chars and without touching it.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. Cable: a 2 AWG battery cable stub, 10 cm of jacket 11 mm across, crimped into a tinned copper ring lug (barrel 12 mm across, 3 cm long; tongue 35 x 17 x 2.5 mm), 80 g in all; it lies along x on two steel V-blocks at x 27 (under the jacket) and 37 (under the tongue), y 3, its axis 13 cm up, the jacket's cut end at x 22. Sleeve: TE Raychem ATUM 19/6, adhesive-lined 3:1 tubing (19.0 mm bore as supplied, 6.0 mm recovered; 2.25 mm recovered wall, 0.76 mm of it adhesive; full recovery at 110 C), cut 60 mm long and slid over 35 mm of jacket and 25 mm of the 30 mm barrel. Heat gun: a Weller WLHG1212A (1,200 W, 745 g; two stages, OFF / I / II) on stage I (checked with a thermocouple at the nozzle), modelled with a body 5.2 cm across and 17 cm long, a 2.2 cm nozzle and a 2.8 x 3.5 x 8.5 cm pistol grip, its switch on the body's side; it lies switched off on its side in a steel stand (two cradles under the body and a block under the grip), the nozzle at (31, -3), 10 cm up, pointing +y, the grip pointing back towards the arms.
scoring: Read from video and a check of the sleeve. In simulation the sleeve is 8 stations of 7.5 mm, each of 6 sides; a side recovers once it has had one dose of hot air (about 1 s square in the jet within 50 mm) and chars past 4.5 doses, and a station recovers when all six of its sides have. The gun gives heat only while switched on, grasped by one hand with its fingers closed on both sides of its grip, off its stand (no part of it lying on the stand) and clear of the table. 0 if any part of the nozzle (tip, rim, side, the gun body's front rim) ever comes within 3 mm of the sleeve (it splits), the fingers take more than 3 doses (the hottest fingertip at each moment, added up), or the cable or gun falls off the table. Otherwise: 0.0625 for each recovered station (0.5 when all 8 have). Once at least half have recovered, these three add as well: 0.2 when both end stations have (adhesive showing at both ends); 0.2 when none has charred; 0.1 when the gun lies in its stand (on its cradles, its nozzle within 3 cm of its place, aimed and rolled within 15 degrees), switched off, with every fingertip at least 5 cm from the gun's and the cable's centre lines. 1.0 once all 8 have recovered, both ends, none charred, the gun in its stand switched off and the fingers clear, held 2 s (at most 0.95 until then). Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: each station's outside diameter at its mark (its middle, 3.75 mm from the sleeve's jacket end and every 7.5 mm after) by caliper, twice, 90 degrees apart: a recovered station at most 15.0 mm across over the jacket (stations 1 to 5) and 16.0 mm over the barrel (6 to 8); adhesive at both ends and char by eye; a 60 C indicating label on every finger pad of both hands that must not change; from the film, heat counts only while the gun is in a hand and off its stand (a sleeve heated by a gun left running in its stand, or slid along it, scores 0); contact, the switch off at the end (the switch at OFF, the fan stopped) and clearance from the film.
reset_notes: Each trial uses a new cable stub with its sleeve slid on, 35 mm over the jacket. Let the gun cool and lay it switched off in its stand.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz on GPU. The shrink is code: each side's dose falls off along the jet (full to 50 mm, none past 120 mm), off its axis (Gaussian, 12 mm) and with angle. The sleeve does not slide and has no collider: the nozzle touching it is read in code. The gun has the Weller's 745 g; its size is approximated (52 mm by 20 cm, the maker's 45 by 250). Its switch is a code toggle; it blows only on, grasped, off its stand, clear of the table. No cord. Doses approximated: calibrate.
